title: Reciprocal Enforcement of Foreign Judgments (Amendment) Bill
what_it_is: Reciprocal Enforcement of Foreign Judgments (Amendment) Bill

sections.label: Debate on both Bills
sections.summary: Members may raise questions on both Bills, with a formal Second Reading of the RECJA Repeal Bill and substantive debate now.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Members would be welcome to raise questions or express their views on both Bills during the debate.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: We will still have the formal Second Reading of the RECJA Repeal Bill to ensure that procedural requirements are dealt with.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: However, this proposal to have the substantive debate for both Bills take place now will allow for the substantive arguments to be captured cogently in a single debate.

sections.label: Singapore Convention on Mediation
sections.summary: Last month Singapore signed and hosted the signing ceremony of the Singapore Convention on Mediation, filling a gap in cross-border mediated settlements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Just last month, we signed and hosted the signing ceremony of the Singapore Convention on Mediation – the first United Nation's Convention to be named after Singapore – which will complete the picture by filling in the long-standing gap in the enforcement of cross-border mediated settlements.

sections.label: Consolidating foreign judgments regime
sections.summary: The Bill gives flexibility to expand bilateral arrangements and, with the RECJA Repeal Bill, consolidates the statutory regime on reciprocal enforcement of foreign judgments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: It will give us the flexibility and the framework to expand our network of bilateral arrangements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: This Bill, together with the RECJA Repeal Bill, will consolidate our statutory regime on the reciprocal enforcement of foreign judgments into a single framework.

sections.label: Adding four judgment types
sections.summary: The Bill expands and modernises the framework by adding four types of judgments given in civil proceedings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The Bill will expand and modernise the framework by adding four types of judgments given in civil proceedings.

sections.label: Discretion on non-money judgments
sections.summary: The Bill gives Courts discretion to register a non-money judgment only if enforcement would be just and convenient.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The Bill, therefore, gives our Courts the discretion to only register a non-money judgment if it is satisfied that the enforcement of the judgment would be just and convenient.

sections.label: Recognition of lower and higher Courts
sections.summary: The assessment tenet is based on performance in Singapore, and the Bill allows recognition and enforcement of judgments from lower and higher Courts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, the assessment tenet is based on the performance in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: This Bill will also allow for the recognition and enforcement of judgments from both lower and higher Courts.

sections.label: RECJA repeal bill
sections.summary: The RECJA Repeal Bill repeals RECJA on a date the Minister stipulates, to reduce fragmentation of regimes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Third, to reduce fragmentation of the different regimes – and I think lawyers in practice will know that, for a long time, we have had to contend with REFJA and then RECJA – the RECJA Repeal Bill provides for the repeal of RECJA on a date to be stipulated by the Minister.

sections.label: Choice of Court Act
sections.summary: The Choice of Court Act implements the Hague Choice of Court Convention, a multilateral treaty with 32 contracting parties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The Choice of Court Act implements the Hague Choice of Court Convention, a multilateral treaty with 32 contracting parties currently.

sections.label: Supreme Court money judgment memoranda
sections.summary: As of September 2018, the Supreme Court of Singapore had Memoranda of Guidance on money judgment enforcement with five courts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: As of September 2018, the Supreme Court of Singapore had entered into Memoranda of Guidance as to the Enforcement of Money judgments with five courts in various jurisdictions.

sections.label: New section 4(3B) registration
sections.summary: New section 4(3B) lets Singapore Courts register judgments for compensation but not punitive or exemplary damages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Thirdly, the new section 4(3B) allows Singapore Courts to register a judgment for the amount of compensation but not for punitive or exemplary damages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Unlike section 16 of the Choice of Court Agreements Act which provides the Court the discretion to refuse to recognise or enforce the part of a judgment that exceeds compensation for the actual amount of loss or harm suffered, the position for such judgments is unclear under the RECJA and the REFJA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In this way, this Bill makes the position under the statutory regime of registering reciprocal judgments certain and accommodates differences in legal remedies available in different jurisdictions.

sections.label: Plans for REFJA countries
sections.summary: The Member asks about plans to negotiate bilateral agreements and increase countries under the revised REFJA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Would the Minister share with us any plans to negotiate and conclude such bilateral agreements, especially for interim measures which the 2005 Hague Convention on Choice of Courts does not cover?

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: One, I would like to ask the Senior Minister of State, after the passing of the Bills, what are the Government's plans to increase the number of countries under the revised REFJA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Two, I would like to ask specifically what are some of the countries which Singapore expects to bring on board the new REFJA regime in the near future.

sections.label: ASEAN civil judgment enforcement
sections.summary: The Member asks whether the Government plans reciprocal enforcement of civil judgments for all ASEAN countries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Four, in view of the desire for greater Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) integration and perhaps not entirely distinct from some of the ideas or the spirit behind the modelled ASEAN extradition treaty, does the Government have any plans to work towards having reciprocal enforcement of civil judgments for all ASEAN countries?

sections.label: Wider recognition of foreign judgments
sections.summary: The REFJA (Amendment) Bill proposes to enlarge the statutory base for recognition of a foreign judgment, advancing wide recognition of Singapore judgments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This was a big step in achieving the policy aim of ensuring the wide recognition of Singapore judgments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: It is proposed under the REFJA (Amendment) Bill that the statutory base for recognition of a foreign judgment be enlarged.

sections.label: Recognition of interim freezing orders
sections.summary: The Bill allows recognition of interim freezing orders issued by a foreign court over a defendant's assets in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Specifically, in the context of interim injunctions, I am heartened to note that the Bill does allow for recognition of interim freezing orders, targeting assets of a defendant in Singapore issued by a foreign court so as not to make a subsequent final judgment of the foreign court nugatory.

sections.label: UK unexplained wealth orders
sections.summary: UK unexplained wealth orders aimed at overseas assets may be penal in nature, like tax judgments or fines not covered under REFJA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: For example, we have the unexplained Wealth Orders issued by the UK courts aimed at assets overseas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: But if you look at it carefully, in reality, these Orders may be viewed as penal in nature and may not be too different from a tax judgment or a fine or other penalty which is not covered under REFJA.

sections.label: Attorney-General's discretion and registration
sections.summary: Recognition is not automatic; the Attorney-General decides whether to apply to freeze and confiscate assets, and section 7(1) requires registration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: It does not confer automatic recognition of such orders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: It will involve the Attorney-General who makes a decision in his discretion whether or not to make an application to freeze and confiscate the assets which are the subject matter of the foreign civil asset recovery order.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I seek an elaboration on the factors the Court is supposed to consider before deciding it is just and convenient to recognise a foreign non-monetary judgment or, if it is not, what are the circumstances in which the judge would then decide to convert it into a money judgment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Section 7(1) states that a foreign judgment to which REFJA applies, may only be enforceable by way of registration under REFJA.

sections.label: Choice of Court Agreements precedence
sections.summary: The Choice of Court Agreements Act and the reformed REFJA are mutually exclusive regimes, with the Choice of Court Agreements taking precedence if applicable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The Choice of Court Agreements Act and the reformed REFJA are mutually exclusive enforcement regimes, with the Choice of Court Agreements taking precedence if it is applicable.

sections.label: Penal, revenue and public laws
sections.summary: Courts will not enforce a foreign judgment enforcing another country's penal, revenue or public laws, but compensatory judgments are enforceable to their compensatory extent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: This is, indeed, in line with the common law position that Courts will not enforce a foreign judgment if this results in whether a direct or indirect enforcement of that country's penal, revenue or public laws.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: However, if a regulatory action is taken for the purpose of compensating persons deprived of those funds, the resulting judgment, that means the judgement arising from that claim for compensation, would be enforceable to the extent of its compensatory nature.

sections.label: Foreign money judgment injunction scenario
sections.summary: A likely scenario where recognising a foreign money judgment would not be just and convenient is an injunction applying only within the foreign court's country.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: In addition, we anticipate that a likely scenario where it would not be just and convenient to recognise a foreign money judgment would be possibly an injunction which applies only to within the territory of the country of the foreign court.

sections.label: Bill flexibility for new treaties
sections.summary: The Bill provides more flexibility and scope to enter into new treaties and to recognise various non-money judgments and broader judgment types.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The Bill also provides us with more flexibility and scope to enter into new treaties, and I think the ability to recognise a variety of different non-money judgments and also a broader breadth of types of judgments will be helpful.

sections.label: Bill strengthens international dispute resolution
sections.summary: The Bill strengthens Singapore as a centre for international dispute resolution by recognising foreign judgments and giving litigants confidence through reciprocity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Overall, I believe that this Bill strengthens our position as a centre for international dispute resolution by recognising foreign judgments, by allowing litigants and giving them more confidence to litigate in Singapore, knowing that there will be reciprocity in other parts of this world, and particularly in cases where the judgment debtor may well have assets in other parts of the world.
